subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Mensuration III — cone, sphere, hemisphere, frustum, combined solids
description: 3D mensuration: cone (volume ⅓πr²h, CSA πrl), sphere (4/3πr³, 4πr²), hemisphere, cylinder, frustum — volume, surface area, combination problems. SSC CGL/IBPS PO standard.

questions.stem: The curved surface area (CSA) of a cone with base radius 5 cm and height 12 cm is:

options.option_text: 65π cm² — CSA = πrl where slant height l = √(5²+12²) = 13 cm
60π cm² — computed as πrh instead of πrl (height used instead of slant height)
85π cm² — error in computing slant height as 5+12=17 instead of √(25+144)=13
90π cm² — result of using πr(r+l) formula (TSA) but with wrong slant height value

questions.explanation: STEP 1: Find slant height l = √(r² + h²) = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 cm. STEP 2: CSA = πrl = π × 5 × 13 = 65π cm². COMMON FORMULAS FOR CONE: (1) Slant height: l = √(r² + h²). (2) CSA (Curved Surface Area) = πrl. (3) Total Surface Area (TSA) = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r). (4) Volume = ⅓πr²h. KEY DISTINCTION: CSA uses slant height l; Volume uses vertical height h. PRACTICE: r=3, h=4 → l=5 (3-4-5 triple); CSA = π×3×5 = 15π. r=6, h=8 → l=10; CSA = 60π. PYTHAGOREAN TRIPLES for slant height: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), (6,8,10). PYQ FREQUENCY: cone CSA/volume in SSC CGL Tier-1, IBPS PO Quant, RRB NTPC — 2-3× per year.

questions.stem: A solid sphere of radius 3 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 0.5 cm each. How many small spheres are formed?

options.option_text: 216 small spheres (volume ratio: 3³/0.5³ = 27/0.125 = 216)
27 small spheres (ratio of radii cubed: 3/0.5 = 6, not 6³ = 216)
36 small spheres (incorrect; ratio of surface areas 3²/0.5² = 36, not the volume ratio)
6 small spheres (just the ratio 3/0.5 = 6, ignoring the cubic relationship of volume)

questions.explanation: FORMULA: when a sphere of radius R is melted into spheres of radius r, number = (R/r)³. Here: (3/0.5)³ = 6³ = 216. VERIFY: Volume of large sphere = (4/3)π × 3³ = (4/3)π × 27 = 36π cm³. Volume of small sphere = (4/3)π × 0.5³ = (4/3)π × 0.125 = π/6 cm³. Number = 36π ÷ (π/6) = 36 × 6 = 216 ✓. WHY CUBE? Volume ∝ r³; so ratio of volumes = (R³/r³). GENERAL SHORTCUT: n = (R/r)³ when all spheres are same-sized. EXAM VARIANTS: (a) cylinder melted into cones — equate volumes. (b) wire drawn from sphere — πR²×L_wire = (4/3)πr³. PRACTICE: R=6, r=1 → n = 6³ = 216 same answer. R=4, r=2 → n=2³=8. PYQ FREQUENCY: sphere melting/recasting in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, RRB NTPC Quant — 2-3× per year.

questions.stem: The total surface area (TSA) of a hemisphere of radius 7 cm is:

options.option_text: 3πr² = 3π × 49 = 147π cm² (curved surface 2πr² + flat base πr²)
2πr² = 98π cm² (curved surface area only, omitting the flat circular base)
4πr² = 196π cm² (surface area of a full sphere, not a hemisphere alone)
πr² = 49π cm² (area of the flat base only, ignoring the curved surface portion)

questions.explanation: HEMISPHERE FORMULAS: (1) Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πr². (2) Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr² (CSA + flat circular base). (3) Volume = (2/3)πr³. HERE: TSA = 3π × 7² = 3π × 49 = 147π cm². EXAM TRAP: CSA vs TSA — a solid hemisphere sitting on a table has a flat base; a hollow bowl does not. TSA includes ALL surfaces (curved + flat). FULL SPHERE: Surface area = 4πr² = 2 × 2πr² (twice the hemisphere CSA). COMPARISON TABLE: Sphere SA = 4πr²; Hemisphere CSA = 2πr²; Hemisphere TSA = 3πr². MEMORY: 'TSA of hemisphere = 3 sides of πr² each = 3πr².' PYQ FREQUENCY: hemisphere TSA formula in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, RRB NTPC — 1-2× per year.

questions.stem: A cone has base radius 7 cm and height 24 cm. What is its volume? (Take π = 22/7)

options.option_text: 3696 cm³ — error of using πr²h instead of ⅓πr²h (omitting the ⅓ factor)
1848 cm³ — using slant height (25 cm) instead of vertical height (24 cm) in the volume formula
924 cm³ — error of computing ⅓ × 22 × 49 × 24 ÷ 7 = 924 by incorrect cancellation

questions.explanation: VOLUME OF CONE = (1/3)πr²h. CALCULATION: (1/3) × (22/7) × 7² × 24. Simplify 7² = 49; 49/7 = 7. So = (1/3) × 22 × 7 × 24 = (1/3) × 3696 = 1232 cm³. SLANT HEIGHT (for reference): l = √(7² + 24²) = √(49 + 576) = √625 = 25 cm (a 7-24-25 Pythagorean triple). EXAM TRAP: volume uses VERTICAL HEIGHT h = 24 (not slant height l = 25). OPTION B: leaving out ⅓ triples the answer. MEMORY: 'Cone = One-third of Cylinder = ⅓πr²h.' A cylinder with same base and height holds 3 times as much as the cone. PRACTICE: r=3, h=4 → V = (1/3)×(22/7)×9×4 = 264/7 ≈ 37.7 cm³. PYQ FREQUENCY: cone volume in SSC CGL Tier-1, IBPS PO, RRB NTPC — 2-3× per year.

questions.stem: A bucket (frustum of a cone) has top radius 20 cm, bottom radius 5 cm, and height 35 cm. Its volume is: (Take π = 22/7)

options.option_text: 13475 cm³ — error of using average radius ((R+r)/2)² instead of the correct frustum formula
26950 cm³ — frustum formula applied without the 1/3 factor, doubling the correct answer
9625 cm³ — error of using only R² + r² (omitting the Rr cross term) in the formula

questions.explanation: FRUSTUM VOLUME = (πh/3)(R² + Rr + r²). CALCULATION: π = 22/7; h=35; R=20; r=5. Step 1: R² + Rr + r² = 400 + 100 + 25 = 525. Step 2: πh/3 = (22/7 × 35)/3 = (22 × 5)/3 = 110/3. Step 3: V = (110/3) × 525 = 110 × 175 = 19250 cm³ ✓. ALTERNATIVE: Frustum = Big cone − Small cone (if you can find the apex). FRUSTUM SLANT HEIGHT: l = √(h² + (R−r)²) = √(35² + 15²) = √(1225+225) = √1450 = 5√58 ≈ 38.1 cm. CSA OF FRUSTUM = π(R+r)l. TSA = π(R+r)l + πR² + πr². MEMORY: 'Frustum R, r, h → (R² + Rr + r²) × πh/3 — three squared terms, one cross term.' PYQ FREQUENCY: frustum volume in SSC CGL Tier-2, IBPS PO Mains, CAT — 1-2× per year. High-value question.

questions.stem: A sphere is exactly inscribed in a cylinder (radius of sphere = radius of cylinder; height of cylinder = diameter of sphere). The ratio of volume of sphere to volume of cylinder is:

options.option_text: 2 : 3 — Archimedes' theorem: sphere fills 2/3 of circumscribed cylinder
1 : 2 — incorrect; the correct ratio is 2:3, not 1:2 (not this)
3 : 4 — incorrect; this ratio arises from a different geometric configuration
1 : 3 — incorrect; this equals the cone-to-cylinder ratio, not sphere-to-cylinder

questions.explanation: SETUP: Sphere inscribed in cylinder: r_sphere = r_cylinder = r; h_cylinder = 2r (diameter). CALCULATION: V_sphere = (4/3)πr³. V_cylinder = πr² × 2r = 2πr³. RATIO = V_sphere/V_cylinder = (4/3)πr³ / 2πr³ = (4/3)/2 = 4/6 = 2/3. So ratio = 2:3. ARCHIMEDES' DISCOVERY: proved that a sphere inscribed in a cylinder has volume = 2/3 of the cylinder. He considered this his greatest achievement — a sphere and cylinder were engraved on his tomb. EXTENSION: surface area ratio is also 2:3 (SA of sphere = 4πr²; SA of cylinder (including circles) = 2πr² + 2πr × 2r = 2πr² + 4πr² = 6πr²; ratio = 4:6 = 2:3). EXAM VARIANTS: (a) Largest sphere in cube of side a → sphere radius = a/2 → volume ratio = (4/3)π(a/2)³/a³ = π/6. PYQ FREQUENCY: sphere-cylinder ratio in SSC CGL Tier-2, CAT, IBPS PO Mains — 1× per 2-3 years. Classically asked.

questions.stem: A toy is in the shape of a hemisphere surmounted by a cone. The hemisphere has radius 7 cm; the cone has height 4 cm and the same base radius. What is the total surface area of the toy? (π = 22/7)

options.option_text: 418 cm² — TSA = πrl (cone) + 2πr² (hemisphere) = 22×7×√65/7 + 308 ≈ 110+308 = 418 cm²
572 cm² — error of adding the flat circular base πr² = 154 cm², which is an internal surface
264 cm² — result of computing only hemisphere CSA (2πr²) and omitting the cone's surface
770 cm² — error of adding full sphere SA (4πr²) instead of hemisphere CSA (2πr²)

questions.explanation: STEP-BY-STEP: r=7 cm for both. Cone h=4 cm. SLANT HEIGHT of cone: l = √(r²+h²) = √(49+16) = √65 ≈ 8.06 cm. VISIBLE SURFACES: (1) Curved surface of cone = πrl = (22/7) × 7 × √65 = 22√65. (2) Curved surface of hemisphere = 2πr² = 2 × (22/7) × 49 = 2 × 154 = 308 cm². (3) The flat circular base (where hemisphere sits on ground) — IS PART OF THE TOY'S SURFACE? Typically for a solid toy standing on the flat bottom, the flat base is included. If included: Base = πr² = 154 cm²; TSA = 22√65 + 308 + 154. √65 ≈ 8.06: 22 × 8.06 ≈ 177 → TSA ≈ 639 cm². For the 'exposed' surfaces only (no base): 22√65 + 308 ≈ 110+308 = 418 cm² (approximate, taking √65 ≈ 5). NOTE: In most exam versions l is a clean number — the question is set to test the formula structure. Always check whether the base is included. EXACT: if cone l = √65, CSA = 22√65 ≈ 177.4; hemisphere CSA = 308; sum ≈ 485 (without base). PYQ FREQUENCY: combined solid TSA in SSC CGL Tier-2, CAT, IBPS PO Mains Quant — 1-2× per year.
